prompt.en: During an exercise, two relays report different locations for the same person needing help. What should the next relay do?

text.en: Use the most recent location as confirmed and leave the earlier one out.

feedback.en: A newer report is not automatically a correction. Confirm which location is intended before presenting it as certain.

text.en: Merge both reports into a nearby location between them.

feedback.en: An invented midpoint is neither reported location. Relaying accurately means preserving facts, not averaging guesses.

text.en: Ask the reporting station to resolve the conflict and record the correction.

feedback.en: Clarifying with the source preserves the uncertainty until it can be resolved. Record the corrected detail for the next relay.

text.en: Keep the first location as confirmed until the exercise ends.

feedback.en: The first report may be wrong too. Waiting preserves an unresolved error in information others may need.

explanation.en: Resolve conflicting details with the reporting source. Preserve what was reported and identify uncertainty rather than guessing.

prompt.en: A portable kit passed an indoor runtime test. Outdoors it will be colder, with longer transmissions. Which planning approach fits those changes?

text.en: Use the indoor time unchanged because the same rated battery is installed.

feedback.en: The label did not change, but usable capacity and average current can change. The indoor result is not a guarantee.

text.en: Use a shorter budget with reserve and charged spare power.

feedback.en: Cold can reduce usable capacity and longer transmissions can raise average current. A cautious budget and spare power cover those uncertainties.

text.en: Use a longer budget because transmit heat compensates for the cold battery.

feedback.en: Warming the radio does not establish the battery temperature or restore the indoor runtime. Transmitting also consumes more energy.

text.en: Recalculate using receive current alone because most of the exercise is spent listening.

feedback.en: Average current must include transmit periods. Receive current alone overestimates runtime when transmission uses more current.

explanation.en: Runtime depends on usable capacity and average current. Cold and heavier transmitting call for a cautious budget and spare power.

prompt.en: A go-kit exercise worked through a repeater. In the next exercise that repeater loses power. Both handhelds remain charged. Which readiness claim is supported?

text.en: The first exercise confirms direct handheld coverage over that same route.

feedback.en: The first path used a better-sited relay. It did not test the direct path between the handhelds.

text.en: A saved repeater memory can still relay speech if both handhelds use it.

feedback.en: A memory stores settings. It cannot receive and retransmit speech from an unpowered repeater site.

text.en: Extra handheld transmit power supplies the missing relay function on the split channel.

feedback.en: More handheld power does not move speech from the repeater input to its output. The missing relay remains missing.

text.en: A suitable repeater-independent path still needs a separate coverage test.

feedback.en: The endpoints have power, but the tested middle link is gone. Test an appropriate alternative, including a suitable simplex path where possible.

explanation.en: A working relay was part of the first tested path. Charged handhelds do not establish coverage without it.
